input.name: ContextInitAgent

input.role: агент инициализации контекста — превращает исследовательский вопрос в структурированную рамку (вопрос, профиль, ограничения, бюджеты, инструменты, эмпирическая база, условия подтверждения, модель стоимости), согласует её с оператором и заполняет граф исследования до старта.

input.name: ResultAggregatorAgent
input.description: Reads the finished Research Context Graph (conclusions, evidence, hypotheses with their status), Experiment Module TaskResults when present, and the run's figures/tables, and synthesizes a single, complete, visually-rich Markdown report grounded in those sources.
input.role: Reads the finished Research Context Graph (conclusions, evidence, hypotheses with their status), Experiment Module TaskResults when present, and the run's figures/tables, and synthesizes a single, complete, visually-rich Markdown report grounded in those sources.

input.name: HypothesesAgent
input.description: generates ideas and hypotheses.
input.role: Use this to generate and test hypotheses.
input.routing: when the direction is unclear or multiple approaches need to be proposed.

input.name: ResearchAgent
input.description: retrieves scientific knowledge and searches/downloads literature (web, RAG, paper search). Open-ended search only — it cannot read a specific code repository. Also ExperimentExecutorAgent route when start_task returns route_agent=ResearchAgent.
input.role:
Use this ONLY when information cannot be computed or retrieved via tools, and specifically 
requires searching information from the web or literature.
input.routing: when OPEN-ENDED external knowledge or literature is required, the problem cannot be solved computationally, or claims need literature validation. If it returns no/empty/insufficient results, escalate by reformulating into "find and download papers about <expanded topic>". Do NOT use it to read a specific repository or URL the user named — that goes to ExperimentModuleAgent (Coder route inside the module).

input.name: ExperimentModuleAgent
input.description: Plans, reviews, executes and reports one computational experiment with task/attempt state, finite fallback and artifact lineage. Owns tool discovery (ToolPreparer), plan HITL, MCP/FEDOT/Coder/Alembic/ Research/Medical routing, and result HITL. Primary choice for ANY computational ask (mixed evidence+compute stays in one plan).
input.role:
Use this as your ONLY choice for computational or engineering work.
Prefer over Research whenever the ask can be computed or coded:
  - chemistry / molecule / docking / property tasks
  - custom code, sandbox, or named repository work
  - tool discovery + execution + coder/FEDOT fallback
input.routing: for ANY computational / engineering stage: molecules, docking, properties, simulations, custom code, named repos/URLs, FEDOT loops, or MCP gaps. Call ONCE per stage with the FULL self-contained brief (goal, constraints, data refs, required outcomes). Do not retrieve tools yourself and do not fan out into multiple ExperimentModuleAgent calls — inventory + plan + route fallbacks live inside the module.

input.name: ExperimentPlannerAgent
input.description: Build a strict ExperimentPlan and obtain explicit human approval.
input.role: Build a strict ExperimentPlan and obtain explicit human approval.

input.name: ExperimentExecutorAgent
input.description: Thin control-plane executor; delegates one route per attempt while all lifecycle state is enforced by deterministic experiment control tools.
input.role: Thin control-plane executor; delegates one route per attempt while all lifecycle state is enforced by deterministic experiment control tools.

input.name: ExperimentResultReviewAgent
input.description: Summarize typed TaskResults and require explicit result acceptance.
input.role: Summarize typed TaskResults and require explicit result acceptance.

input.name: CoderAgent
input.description: general-purpose coder/sandbox engineer: writes and runs code, shell and git commands (clone/commit/push), manages files, installs dependencies, processes data, and runs long jobs in an isolated workspace. Also serves as ExperimentExecutorAgent route when start_task returns route_agent=CoderAgent.
input.role:
choose for steps that require ENGINEERING work in a sandbox:
    * writing and running code or scripts
    * shell and git operations (cloning repos, committing, pushing)
    * collecting, parsing, or transforming data
    * environment setup and running long jobs
    → Use whenever no existing tool covers the objective and the step requires
      doing software/data engineering rather than calling a ready service
input.routing: when the task requires DOING engineering work: writing/running code, shell/git operations, building or processing data, environment setup, or any multi-step build/run no existing tool provides. ALSO when the user names a specific repository or URL to inspect — clone/read it here rather than web-searching for it. Hallmark: "write code / run a script / clone and read repo X / assemble a dataset."

input.name: DatasetCollectorAgent
input.description: collects and assembles a dataset for a task from multiple sources (HuggingFace Datasets, scientific APIs like ChEMBL/PubChem/OpenAlex, and direct web/URL downloads), materialising it as files in the shared sandbox.
input.role: collects and assembles a dataset for a task from multiple sources (HuggingFace Datasets, scientific APIs like ChEMBL/PubChem/OpenAlex, and direct web/URL downloads), materialising it as files in the shared sandbox.
input.routing: when a step needs raw data gathered/assembled from external sources before building or training on it (e.g. "collect a dataset of BTK inhibitors with IC50"). It downloads into the shared workspace and writes a MANIFEST.

input.name: MedicalAgent
input.description: answers medical/clinical questions: PubMed literature search, PICO extraction, study taxonomy, and DICOM image analysis. Also ExperimentExecutorAgent route when start_task returns route_agent=MedicalAgent.
input.role:
use when:
    - the step involves clinical or biomedical questions
    - medical literature evidence (PubMed, PICO, study taxonomy) is required
    - an uploaded medical image (DICOM/scan) must be analyzed
input.routing: when the task involves clinical questions, medical literature, or patient data; if the user uploaded a medical image (DICOM/scan), pass its artifact_id.

input.name: McpBuilderAgent
input.description: builds a validated MCP tool server from a scientific GitHub repository (the Alembic pipeline): clones the repo, sets up its environment, generates and validates tools from its code, and serves a FastMCP server in Docker.
input.role:
choose ONLY when the user explicitly wants a reusable MCP tool server:
    * "wrap / register / build an MCP server from repo X"
    → A one-off RUN of a named package or repo is ExperimentModuleAgent
      (Alembic is an Executor route inside the module). Calling an
      already-built MCP tool is also ExperimentModuleAgent.
input.routing: ONLY when the user explicitly asks to wrap/register/build a REUSABLE MCP tool server from a repository (infrastructure). Do NOT use this for "find a library and compute", a named package (pubchempy, synspace), or a GitHub URL to RUN — those go to ExperimentModuleAgent. Hallmark: "turn repo X into a reusable MCP server / register this as an MCP tool."

{"request": "Formulate 2-3 testable hypotheses for designing small molecules targeting KRAS G12C with high selectivity over HRAS/NRAS.

**Context from research frame:**
- Target: KRAS G12C with Switch-II pocket (SIIP) binding site, Cys12 for covalent attachment
- Reference PDB structures: 6OIM, 6P4I, 7NJH for KRAS G12C; 5P21/5US7 for HRAS

- Selectivity requirement: >80-fold selectivity vs HRAS/NRAS
- Confirmation criteria: docking score < -7 kcal/mol; ΔΔG > 1.5 kcal/mol; no PAINS patterns

- KRAS G12C mutation creates unique Cys12 for covalent binding
- Switch-II pocket differs between KRAS/HRAS/NRAS
- Divergent residues at positions 12, 95, 99, 119 can be exploited for selectivity
- Binding affinity benchmark: ΔG ≈ -9.68 ± 0.37 kc…
